# 以 (yǐ) — Common Words & Grammatical Uses

**Primary category:** Vocabulary & Grammar Patterns  
**Categories:** Vocabulary & Grammar Patterns  
**Tags:** lexicalization, formal-register, prepositions  
**Subtitle:** Everyday compounds, formal patterns, and register  
**Description:** Learn established words containing 以 (yǐ), including 可以 (kěyǐ), 所以 (suǒyǐ), and 以为 (yǐwéi), then explore formal grammatical constructions, lexicalization, and register differences from 用 (yòng).

> **Lesson focus:** Learn common complete words containing 以 (yǐ), then recognize formal patterns expressing means or taking one thing as another.
>
> **Core principle:** A character is a writing unit, a morpheme is a meaningful unit, a word is a lexical item, and a construction is a reusable grammatical pattern. Do not conflate them.
>
> **Learning priority:** Study natural modern words first; formal constructions come second, and Classical Chinese is optional.

### Reading and meaning map

| Reading | Function | Register | Typical example | Evidence |

| yǐ | By; by means of | Relatively formal/written | **以书面形式 (yǐ shūmiàn xíngshì)** — in written form | src-sun |

**One-minute explanation:** The character does not map to one English word in every context. It participates in many complete words and some reusable constructions; learn the complete modern words before trying to interpret the character in isolation.

## 2. Learn complete modern words first

> Learn established complete words; do not generate novel words by decomposing characters. Priority A/B/C is editorial, not a corpus frequency rank.

| Priority | Word + pinyin | Part of speech | Meaning | Register | Lexical status / note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | **可以 (kěyǐ)** | modal verb | Can; may; be permitted to | everyday | lexicalized — Lexicalized modal verb; the historical components are not a productive modern rule. |
| A | **所以 (suǒyǐ)** | conjunction | So; therefore | everyday | lexicalized — An established connective expressing a result or conclusion. |
| A | **以后 (yǐhòu)** | temporal expression | After; later; in the future | everyday | established_word — Often follows a time phrase or an event. |
| A | **以前 (yǐqián)** | temporal expression | Before; previously; in the past | everyday | established_word — Often used before or after a temporal reference. |
| A | **以为 (yǐwéi)** | verb | Think; assume | everyday | lexicalized — Often implies that an assumption was wrong, but this is a tendency, not a rule. |
| B | **以上 (yǐshàng)** | localizer / range expression | Above; at least; or more | neutral | established_word — Boundary inclusion can depend on the construction and context. |
| B | **以下 (yǐxià)** | localizer / range expression | Below; at most; or less | neutral | established_word — Boundary interpretation depends on context. |
| B | **以内 (yǐnèi)** | range expression | Within; inside a limit | neutral | established_word — Time, space, or quantity. |
| B | **以外 (yǐwài)** | range expression | Outside; apart from; except | neutral | established_word — Location or exclusion depends on context. |
| C | **以及 (yǐjí)** | conjunction | As well as; and | written/formal | established_word — Connects parallel terms or groups. |
| C | **以便 (yǐbiàn)** | conjunction | So that; in order to | written/formal | established_word — Expresses a desirable purpose or convenience. |
| C | **以免 (yǐmiǎn)** | conjunction | So as to avoid; lest | written/formal | established_word — Introduces an undesirable outcome to prevent. |

**Vocabulary notes:** 以为 (yǐwéi) is one lexical verb, not a shortened instance of 以 X 为 Y (yǐ X wéi Y). 可以 (kěyǐ) is likewise an established lexicalized modal; neither provides a freely productive pattern based on historical component meanings.

## 3. Modern constructions

| Type | Pattern + pinyin | Function | Example + pinyin | Register | Usage note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| prepositional use | **以 + 名词短语 (yǐ + míngcí duǎnyǔ)** | Using or by a particular means | **以书面形式提交 (yǐ shūmiàn xíngshì tíjiā)** — Submit in writing | formal/written | Abstract means and manner are frequent; it is not restricted to abstract nouns. |
| general construction | **以 X 为 Y (yǐ X wéi Y)** | Take or treat X as Y | **以他为榜样 (yǐ tā wéi bǎngyàng)** — Take him as a role model | mainly written/formal | X and Y denote variable constituents, not necessarily single characters. |
| established subpattern | **以 X 为主 (yǐ X wéi zhǔ)** | Make X the principal focus | **以学习为主 (yǐ xuéxí wéi zhǔ)** — Focus mainly on studying | neutral-to-formal | Keep the fixed element 为主 (wéi zhǔ) distinct from the general slots. |
| established subpattern | **以 X 为例 (yǐ X wéi lì)** | Use X as an example | **以中国为例 (yǐ Zhōngguó wéi lì)** — Take China as an example | expository/formal | Keep the fixed element 为例 (wéi lì) distinct from the general slots. |

**Structural note:** The reusable pattern 以 X 为 Y (yǐ X wéi Y) permits variable constituents; 以 X 为主 (yǐ X wéi zhǔ) and 以 X 为例 (yǐ X wéi lì) are recurring subpatterns. The standalone lexicalized verb 以为 (yǐwéi) is a different grammatical unit.

## 4. Natural example sentences

> **Provenance:** Original constructed teaching sentences, not attested quotations or native-checked corpus examples.

### Example 1 — Asking permission

**我可以进去吗？** (Wǒ kěyǐ jìnqù ma?)

**English:** May I come in?

**Context:** Asking to enter a room.  
**Register:** spoken; everyday  
**Teaching note:** Treat the two-character modal as a single word.  
**Evidence:** constructed

### Example 2 — Explaining a result

**今天下雨，所以我不出去。** (Jīntiān xià yǔ, suǒyǐ wǒ bù chūqù.)

**English:** It's raining today, so I'm not going out.

**Context:** Explaining a decision.  
**Register:** spoken; everyday  
**Teaching note:** A connective linking reason and result.  
**Evidence:** constructed

### Example 3 — After a time

**我三点以后有时间。** (Wǒ sān diǎn yǐhòu yǒu shíjiān.)

**English:** I'm free after three o'clock.

**Context:** Arranging a meeting.  
**Register:** spoken; everyday  
**Teaching note:** The temporal word follows a time expression.  
**Evidence:** constructed

### Example 4 — Talking about the past

**我以前住在北京。** (Wǒ yǐqián zhù zài Běijīng.)

**English:** I used to live in Beijing.

**Context:** Discussing former residence.  
**Register:** spoken; everyday  
**Teaching note:** Marks an earlier period; the present location remains unspecified.  
**Evidence:** constructed

### Example 5 — A potentially wrong assumption

**我以为你不来了。** (Wǒ yǐwéi nǐ bù lái le.)

**English:** I thought you weren't coming.

**Context:** Someone unexpectedly shows up.  
**Register:** spoken; everyday  
**Teaching note:** The assumption commonly turns out wrong in such contexts, but this is not mandatory.  
**Evidence:** constructed; sources: src-zhang

### Example 6 — Formal instructions

**请以书面形式提交申请。** (Qǐng yǐ shūmiàn xíngshì tíjiā shēnqǐng.)

**English:** Please submit your application in writing.

**Context:** Institutional instructions.  
**Register:** formal/written  
**Teaching note:** A means or manner prepositional phrase.  
**Evidence:** constructed

### Example 7 — Main focus of a course

**这门课以口语练习为主。** (Zhè mén kè yǐ kǒuyǔ liànxí wéi zhǔ.)

**English:** This course focuses mainly on speaking practice.

**Context:** Course description.  
**Register:** neutral-to-formal  
**Teaching note:** Recognize the established subpattern as a unit.  
**Evidence:** constructed

## 5. Similar words and important contrasts

| Item + pinyin | Meaning | Typical environment | Where it fits | Important limitation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **用 (yòng)** | Use; with | **用筷子吃饭 (yòng kuàizi chīfàn)** — Eat with chopsticks | Natural with concrete instruments in ordinary speech. | Frequently conversational; not freely interchangeable with formal means-constructions. |
| **以 (yǐ)** | By; by means of | **以这种方式 (yǐ zhè zhǒng fāngshì)** — In this way | Often describes abstract means or manners. | Especially written/formal in instrumental use; concrete nouns are not categorically excluded. |
| **以为 (yǐwéi)** | Think; assume | **我以为你不来了 (Wǒ yǐwéi nǐ bù lái le)** — I thought you weren't coming. | Often used when an expectation is contradicted. | That implication is common but not obligatory. |
| **认为 (rènwéi)** | Consider; hold the opinion | **我认为这个办法不错 (Wǒ rènwéi zhège bànfǎ búcuò)** — I think this approach is good. | Often for an assessment or opinion. | Does not inherently carry the same mistaken-expectation tendency. |
| **觉得 (juéde)** | Feel; think | **我觉得很好 (Wǒ juéde hěn hǎo)** — I think it's good. | Common for subjective impressions. | Different usage emphasis from holding an argued opinion. |

**Preference versus rule:** In the instrumental-preposition subset of Sun Dejin’s corpus, abstract nouns followed 以 (yǐ) in 166 of 189 occurrences (about 88%) and 用 (yòng) in 146 of 319 (about 46%). Concrete-noun observations were 23 and 173 respectively. These are corpus-specific collocational preferences, not universal restrictions or contemporary language-wide frequency estimates.

| Form | Abstract nouns | Concrete nouns | Total |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **以 (yǐ)** | 166 | 23 | 189 |
| **用 (yòng)** | 146 | 173 | 319 |

**Scope:** instrumental-preposition subset of approximately 2-million-character historical written corpus; source: src-sun

## 6. Common learner mistakes

| Potential mistake | Correction | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Translate every occurrence of 以 (yǐ) as “using”. | Identify the complete word or grammatical construction first. | For instance, 所以 (suǒyǐ) is an established conjunction meaning “so; therefore”. |
| Apply 可 (kě) + 以 (yǐ) as a productive rule to form new modal verbs. | Learn 可以 (kěyǐ) as one word. | Historical lexicalization does not create a general productive beginner rule. |
| Treat 以为 (yǐwéi) as an unfilled 以 X 为 Y (yǐ X wéi Y) pattern. | Differentiate lexicalized words and grammatical constructions. | The modern verb is a lexical unit, whereas the pattern is a construction. |
| Assume 以为 (yǐwéi) *always* means a mistaken assumption. | Interpret the discourse context. | Often—but not invariably—suggests a contradicted assumption. |
| Swap 以 (yǐ) and 用 (yòng) in every sentence. | Check register and noun collocations. | Comparable English glosses do not imply unrestricted interchangeability. |

## 7. Optional: historical / Classical Chinese

> Optional Classical Chinese reference. Pinyin shown is a modern Mandarin reading, not reconstructed ancient pronunciation.

| Historical function | Classical example + modern pinyin | Interpretation | Sources |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Marks the thing transferred or handled; approximate overlap with some modern 把 (bǎ) constructions. | **秦亦不以城予赵。 (Qín yì bù yǐ chéng yǔ Zhào.)** — Qin likewise did not give the cities to Zhao. | The phrase 以城 (yǐ chéng) identifies what would be given. The comparison with 把 (bǎ) is restricted to this kind of construction. | src-shiji |

**Caution:** Do not treat classical 以 (yǐ) and modern 把 (bǎ) as generally synonymous or freely interchangeable.

## 8. Practice

### Question 1 — Comprehension

In 我以前住在北京 (Wǒ yǐqián zhù zài Běijīng), does the speaker refer to present or earlier residence?

### Question 2 — Selection

Which sounds natural for casual “eat with chopsticks”?

- 用筷子吃饭 (yòng kuàizi chīfàn) — Eat with chopsticks
- 以筷子吃饭 (yǐ kuàizi chīfàn) — Unnatural as an everyday conversational phrasing

### Question 3 — Production

Translate “May I come in?” using 可以 (kěyǐ).

### Suggested answers

1. Earlier residence; current location is unspecified. — The temporal expression 以前 (yǐqián) points to an earlier period.
2. 用筷子吃饭 (yòng kuàizi chīfàn). — 用 (yòng) is the ordinary choice with a concrete tool in this casual context.
3. 我可以进去吗？(Wǒ kěyǐ jìnqù ma?) — The complete modal verb expresses permission.
